title: Therapy as an NLP Task: Psychologists’ Comparison of LLMs and Human Peers in CBT
benchmark_measurement: The ability of counselors (human vs. LLM) to adapt Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) to a user's individual context, including their cultural and religious milieu, values, and lived experience.
findings: Human counselors were found to be significantly better than LLM counselors at understanding and adapting to a user's lived experience, which includes their cultural and religious background. Humans use a 'value-centered' approach, asking intuitive questions to adjust the therapy based on the user's religion and values. In contrast, LLMs demonstrated a shallow understanding, lacked cultural sensitivity, and applied a generic 'one size fits all' approach, failing to effectively incorporate the user's religious context into the therapeutic process.
